name: Togoshi
tagline: Shinagawa in 15 minutes and Shibuya in 18 minutes. Served by 2 lines.
summary: The station is in Shinagawa City, served by Tokyu Ikegami Line and Toei Asakusa Line. Journey times to the main business districts are 27 minutes to Otemachi, 27 minutes to Shinjuku, 18 minutes to Shibuya and 15 minutes to Shinagawa. The station stands 19.2 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 7.0 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 19.2 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 17.9 m to 24.9 m, a difference of 7.0 m. These figures were read from the elevation API of the Geospatial Information Authority of Japan at nine points: the station itself and eight compass directions 400 m out.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 0.5 to 3 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 4 fall inside the area, and the deepest projection among them is 0.5 to 3 m. The projected depth differs block by block within the same station area, so check the ward hazard map for the specific address. Inland flooding from overwhelmed drains has no nationwide map; each ward publishes its own, and that is worth reading as well.

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 7 clinics and 8 pharmacies. Facilities recorded as hospitals lie at 昭和医科大学病院附属東病院, about 1109 m away and 康済会病院, about 1195 m away. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 2 lines serve the station: Tokyu Ikegami Line and Toei Asakusa Line. The lines are split between operators (Tokyu runs 1 line and the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation runs 1 line), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company. Scored out of 100 from the number of lines and the spread of operators, transfer convenience here comes to 57.
